gen.title: Strategies, shifts and limits in the fight for voting rights

cards.stem: What reason does the text give for many women remaining unable to vote long into the 20th century?
cards.quote: Many women remained unable to vote long into the 20th century because of discriminatory state voting laws.
cards.hint: Look for the cause mentioned after ratification.

cards.stem: Which approach did some supporters use to win voting rights before a federal amendment?
cards.quote: Some pursued a strategy of passing suffrage acts in each state—nine western states adopted woman suffrage legislation by 1912.
cards.hint: Recall how many western states adopted legislation by 1912.

cards.stem: Whose change to support an amendment in 1918 helped shift the political balance?
cards.quote: President Wilson changed his position to support an amendment in 1918, the political balance began to shift.
cards.hint: Consider the national leader who changed position in 1918.

cards.stem: What share of states had to agree for the amendment to clear its final hurdle?
options: a simple majority of the states
cards.quote: the amendment passed its final hurdle of obtaining the agreement of three-fourths of the states.
cards.hint: Think about the fraction required for ratification.
